newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber ends down, covering for RSS3 seen.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber ends down, covering for RSS3 seen.

text.p: Rubber futures closed slightly easier on Thursday in a listless market, except for moderate covering seen in RSS3 rubber, dealers said.

"The action in the market was almost non-existent. The only bright spot was provided by the late covering for RSS3 rubber. It was extremely thin in the other brands and the trade was very, very quiet," a trader for a foreign dealing house said.
The fall in Tokyo's benchmark August contract, which settled 1.0 yen down to 150.8, weighed on market sentiment.
"We're really looking for inspiration today. Aside from RSS3, there was nothing else in the market," a trader said.
Some 6,600 tonnes of prompt shipment RSS3 rubber was traded. The volume, however, for RSS1 and TSR20 rubber barely exceeded 600 tonnes, traders said.
At around 0945 GMT, April RSS3 was seen at 120.00-122.00 U.S. cents a kg from the previous 122.00 cents.
April RSS1 was indicated at 171.00-173.00 Singapore cents (US$1.20-$1.22) a kg from the previous 173.25 cents.
April TSR20 was indicated unchanged at 169.50 Singapore cents (US$1.19) a kg.
